sources.title_original: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 release candidate
sources.recommend_reason_zh: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 候选版发布，可在气隙环境的设备CPU上运行自包含AI模型检测非结构化密钥，无需GPU或外联，并让Dependabot默认等包版本发布满三天才提更新PR。

en.reason: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 runs a self-contained AI model on device CPUs to detect unstructured secrets in air-gapped networks without GPUs or external connectivity, and makes Dependabot wait three days after a package version's release before opening update PRs.

sources.title: 对抗性蒸馏的应对之道 / Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.title_zh: 对抗性蒸馏的应对之道
sources.title_en: Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.title_original: Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.recommend_reason_zh: OpenAI 介绍其对抗 adversarial distillation 的分层防护，并称 GPT‑6.2 Astra 与 GPT‑6.2 Sol 已强化 protected reasoning 防护，内部红队评估平均攻击成功率从 54.0% 降至 0.2%。

en.reason: OpenAI’s layered defenses against adversarial distillation, spanning model training, safeguards, detection and enforcement, cut internal red-team average attack success from 54.0% to 0.2% for GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol’s protected reasoning.

stories.title: ByteDance 认为大多数 AI 训练阶段并无必要，并用一个有竞争力的开源模型证明了这一点 / Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model

sources.title: ByteDance 认为大多数 AI 训练阶段并无必要，并用一个有竞争力的开源模型证明了这一点 / Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model

sources.title_en: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
sources.title_original: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
sources.summary:
Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The researchers attribute the gains to carefully curated training data rather than ever more training steps. The model, data, and code are freely available.
Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three tr

en.reason: Bytedance and several US universities released Axion 1.0, an AI agent that matches OpenAI and Anthropic commercial models on benchmarks after only three training phases, crediting curated data over more steps and open-sourcing model, data and code.

en.title: Damn — former Google CEO Eric Schmidt just spent 27 seconds laying out the easiest route to getting rich over the next two years. Making money, it turns out, is simple: start an agentic AI company, build an agent that can actually do real work, and own the whole thing yourself. From prompts, memory and skills to MCP, plus dev tools like Claude Code, one person can hand-build a company inside the one-to-two-year window. But after spending my days lately wrangling every kind of Agent workflow, I've grown increasingly clear-eyed: plenty of people are working themselves ragged building memory into AI, …
en.reason: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt’s 27-second path to wealth in the next two years centers on founding an agentic AI company you fully own, built solo with prompts, memory, skills, MCP and tools like Claude Code, while the piece warns that late nights, takeout and unchecked blood lipids and glucose can crash your body before your agent ships.

stories.title: AI 的记忆在帮我，也好像困住了我

sources.title: AI 的记忆在帮我，也好像困住了我
sources.title_zh: AI 的记忆在帮我，也好像困住了我
sources.title_original: AI 的记忆在帮我，也好像困住了我
sources.summary: AI记忆带来便捷的同时，也暗藏困住人的风险。作者因写入“小白讲师”标签，导致AI持续把机会局限在培训赛道，不断强化刻板印象，甚至让自己慢慢认同这个单一身份。这篇思考给高频使用 Agent 的人也敲了警钟，提醒我们在人机共生中，别让 AI 的记忆框住自己更多潜在方向。
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 每天用AI记忆，因‘小白讲师’标签只收到培训建议；AI查半导体国产替代6个环节、约50家公司，结论只剩国产GPU开发者生态和请外部讲师两个口子，反思记忆框住自我。

en.title: AI memory is helping me — and also seems to trap me
en.summary: AI memory brings convenience, but it also carries a hidden risk of trapping people. After the author added a "novice lecturer" tag, the AI kept limiting opportunities to the training track, reinforcing the stereotype and even leading the author to gradually identify with this single identity. This reflection is a warning for heavy Agent users: in human-AI coexistence, don't let AI's memory box in your broader potential.

en.title: How do you test AI visibility in GEO? Recording cards as a case study
en.summary: To find out whether AI will proactively recommend your product, this reusable AI visibility testing method is worth a look. Using Notta Memo’s overseas market test as a case study and drawing on NIST and IAB industry standards, the author explains prompt design, variable control, result evaluation, baseline retention, and retesting logic, with a logging template included.
en.reason: Using Notta Memo's US-English launch as a case study, the piece lays out a reusable GEO testing method built on NIST and IAB standards, covering prompt design, variable control, distinguishing brand mentions from product recommendations, and baseline logs for retesting.

en.title: Grab uses security policies to tackle a surge in AI-generated code changes, boosting mobile app stability
en.reason: Grab built a layered, left-shifted defense across its mobile release lifecycle—using Android Lint and SwiftLint before merge plus GEA pre-production gates and staged rollout—to prevent, detect and isolate crashes as AI-assisted coding inflates per-release code changes.

stories.title: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀

sources.title: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
sources.title_zh: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
sources.title_original: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
sources.summary:
AI 读不懂代码，多半是注释只写了「做什么」。四类高价值注释补上意图、边界与取舍，曲解、过度优化、上下文膨胀一起降。
核心结论 ：模型读代码时，除了语法结构，唯一能拿到的「意图信息」就是注释和命名。命名只能承载「它叫什么」，注释才能承载「为什么这么写、不能怎么改」。所以关键注释不是给人看的礼貌，而是给模型看的接口——写清契约、陷阱、不变量，模型就不会把只读函数当纯函数改、不会顺手「优化」掉有副作用的分支、不会在缺信息时反复猜测，也不用通读三百行才明白设计意图。
AI 改代码出错的多数场景，不是它不会写，而是它 理解错了这段代码的意图 。而意图不在语法里，在注释里。
一句「这里必须加锁，否则并发下会重复扣款」，能让模型避开一整类错误；一句「先别改成批量查询，这个接口有顺序依赖」，能省掉三轮返工。这两句话的成本是二十来个 token，收益是省下一次 review 加一次回滚。
模型拿到一个文件时，能读到的信息分两层：
结构层是精确的，但语义是压缩的。 def fetch_user(uid) 读不出它会不会写缓存、会不会抛异常、并发下安不安全——这些恰好是改代码时最容易踩的地方。命名能补一点
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章用契约、陷阱、不变量、取舍四类注释让AI读懂代码意图，并算清40 token契约注释省约6000 token返工的150倍账。

en.title: When AI Can't Read Your Code: Using High-Value Comments to Eliminate Misinterpretation, Over-Optimization, and Context Bloat
en.summary:
When AI fails to understand code, it’s usually because comments only say what it does. Four kinds of high-value comments fill in intent, boundaries, and trade-offs, cutting misinterpretation, over-optimization, and context bloat at once.

Core takeaway: When a model reads code, apart from syntax, the only intent information it gets is comments and naming. Naming can only convey what something is called; comments are what convey why it was written this way and how it must not be changed. Key comments are therefore not politeness for humans but an interface for the model: spell out contracts, traps, and invariants, and the model won’t treat a read-only function as pure and change it, won’t casually optimize away a branch with side effects, won’t keep guessing when information is missing, and won’t need to read 300 lines to understand the design intent.

In most cases where AI errs while changing code, it isn’t that it can’t write code; it has misread the intent of that code. And intent isn’t in the syntax—it’s in the comments.

A single comment saying a lock is required here or concurrent requests will double-charge can help the model avoid an entire class of errors; a comment saying don’t change this to a batch query yet because the interface has order dependencies can save three rounds of rework. These two sentences cost about 20 tokens and save a review plus a rollback.

When a model gets a file, the information it can read falls into two layers:

The structural layer is precise, but the semantics are compressed. From def fetch_user(uid), it can’t tell whether the function writes to a cache, throws exceptions, or is safe under concurrency—exactly the places where code changes most often go wrong. Naming can fill in a little.
en.reason: Four kinds of comments—contract, trap, invariant and trade-off—give AI the intent that syntax and naming cannot, and a 40-token contract comment can save roughly 6,000 tokens of rework, a 150x return.

primary_item.title: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
primary_item.title_zh: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
primary_item.title_original: AI 读不懂你的代码怎么办：用高价值注释消除曲解、过度优化与上下文膨胀
primary_item.summary:
AI 读不懂代码，多半是注释只写了「做什么」。四类高价值注释补上意图、边界与取舍，曲解、过度优化、上下文膨胀一起降。
核心结论 ：模型读代码时，除了语法结构，唯一能拿到的「意图信息」就是注释和命名。命名只能承载「它叫什么」，注释才能承载「为什么这么写、不能怎么改」。所以关键注释不是给人看的礼貌，而是给模型看的接口——写清契约、陷阱、不变量，模型就不会把只读函数当纯函数改、不会顺手「优化」掉有副作用的分支、不会在缺信息时反复猜测，也不用通读三百行才明白设计意图。
AI 改代码出错的多数场景，不是它不会写，而是它 理解错了这段代码的意图 。而意图不在语法里，在注释里。
一句「这里必须加锁，否则并发下会重复扣款」，能让模型避开一整类错误；一句「先别改成批量查询，这个接口有顺序依赖」，能省掉三轮返工。这两句话的成本是二十来个 token，收益是省下一次 review 加一次回滚。
模型拿到一个文件时，能读到的信息分两层：
结构层是精确的，但语义是压缩的。 def fetch_user(uid) 读不出它会不会写缓存、会不会抛异常、并发下安不安全——这些恰好是改代码时最容易踩的地方。命名能补一点

en.title: When AI Can't Read Your Code: Using High-Value Comments to Eliminate Misinterpretation, Over-Optimization, and Context Bloat
en.summary:
When AI fails to understand code, it’s usually because comments only say what it does. Four kinds of high-value comments fill in intent, boundaries, and trade-offs, cutting misinterpretation, over-optimization, and context bloat at once.

Core takeaway: When a model reads code, apart from syntax, the only intent information it gets is comments and naming. Naming can only convey what something is called; comments are what convey why it was written this way and how it must not be changed. Key comments are therefore not politeness for humans but an interface for the model: spell out contracts, traps, and invariants, and the model won’t treat a read-only function as pure and change it, won’t casually optimize away a branch with side effects, won’t keep guessing when information is missing, and won’t need to read 300 lines to understand the design intent.

In most cases where AI errs while changing code, it isn’t that it can’t write code; it has misread the intent of that code. And intent isn’t in the syntax—it’s in the comments.

A single comment saying a lock is required here or concurrent requests will double-charge can help the model avoid an entire class of errors; a comment saying don’t change this to a batch query yet because the interface has order dependencies can save three rounds of rework. These two sentences cost about 20 tokens and save a review plus a rollback.

When a model gets a file, the information it can read falls into two layers:

The structural layer is precise, but the semantics are compressed. From def fetch_user(uid), it can’t tell whether the function writes to a cache, throws exceptions, or is safe under concurrency—exactly the places where code changes most often go wrong. Naming can fill in a little.

今年 9 月底 Google 首次公布了 Gemini 4 Argon ，并在 10 月 13 日 向所有用户全面开放。随后的更新节奏很紧凑：定位更高的 Gemini 4 Carbon 在 10 月底亮相、11 月 10 日全面上线，主打速度的轻量模型 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 也在 11 月 12 日紧跟着发布了。

en.title: Hands-On with the Gemini 4 Series and Antigravity: Carbon, Argon, and Hydrogen Tested, Plus Speed-Up Tips
en.summary:
Real-world impressions after a month of heavy use of Gemini 4 and Antigravity: how Carbon, Argon, and Hydrogen differ, where Claude and GPT fall short and where they win, plus tips for controlling style and reading code faster.

Google first unveiled Gemini 4 Argon in late September and opened it to all users on October 13. The release cadence has been tight since: the higher-positioned Gemini 4 Carbon appeared in late October and went fully live on November 10, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a lightweight model built for speed, followed on November 12.

Before getting into the hands-on impressions, here are the current official API prices for the three models (all support a 1M Token context, and output billing includes thinking Tokens):

As you can see, Carbon and Argon carry exactly the same list price per unit, and once original pricing returns in December, calling the API pay-as-you-go for heavy development won't be cheap. Since Argon went fully live, I've been on the $200 plan in Google's AI coding tool Antigravity and have used it intensively for over a month. This article draws on that daily hands-on work to…
en.reason: A month of high-intensity testing inside Antigravity on a $200 plan compares Gemini 4 Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen, covering their identical Carbon/Argon API pricing, 1M-token context, and a Codex Review workaround for Carbon's slow code reading.

stories.title: OpenClaw 退潮背后，是 AI 圈“技术自嗨”的终结

sources.title: OpenClaw 退潮背后，是 AI 圈“技术自嗨”的终结
sources.title_zh: OpenClaw 退潮背后，是 AI 圈“技术自嗨”的终结
sources.title_original: OpenClaw 退潮背后，是 AI 圈“技术自嗨”的终结
sources.summary:
OpenClaw 两个月狂揽 27 万 GitHub 星标后迅速退潮：安装像一堆散装零件，Token 成本失控，安全权限模糊甚至误删邮件。它提醒行业，别再技术自嗨，要把门槛、成本和安全性做扎实。
原文： mp.weixin.qq.com/s/yo4X5dK45… （2026年04月26日）
2026 年初，如果你在互联网圈混，肯定躲不过一只名叫 OpenClaw 的“科技龙虾”。
两个月内，它在 GitHub 上狂揽 27 万星标，直接把 Linux 的历史纪录踩在脚下；大厂疯抢，朋友圈刷屏，仿佛你不“养只虾”，出门都不好意思跟同行打招呼。
但互联网的记忆就是这么魔幻。
仅仅两个月后，画风突变。第一批跟风“养虾”的人，已经开始花钱请人卸载了；工信部直接下发安全预警；各路科技媒体纷纷倒戈，直呼“能力不足、成本太高”。
这场来得快去得也快的技术狂欢，其实在很多业内老司机看来，完全是意料之中。说句扎心的话： OpenClaw 本质上就是一个 toy（玩具）级别的 AI 概念机，离真正的生产力工具差了十万八千里。
为什么这么说？咱们今天不聊晦涩的代码，只聊业务和常识。
OpenClaw爆火场景
sources.recommend_reason_zh: OpenClaw 两个月揽下27万GitHub星标后迅速退潮，安装复杂、Token费一月可烧上万元，Meta安全总监还被它误删邮件，文章借此剖析AI技术自嗨的终结。

en.title: OpenClaw's Decline Marks the End of the AI World's Self-Indulgent Tech Era
en.summary:
After racking up 270,000 GitHub stars in two months, OpenClaw is beating a fast retreat: installation feels like assembling a pile of loose parts, Token costs are out of control, security permissions are murky, and it has even deleted emails by mistake. The episode is a reminder to the industry: stop the tech self-indulgence and get onboarding, cost, and security right.

Original: mp.weixin.qq.com/s/yo4X5dK45… (April 26, 2026)

In early 2026, anyone in internet circles could hardly avoid a "tech lobster" named OpenClaw.

Within two months it pulled in 270,000 GitHub stars, trampling Linux's all-time record; big tech scrambled for it, it flooded WeChat Moments, and it felt as if you couldn't greet a peer without "raising a lobster."

But the internet's memory is a strange thing.

Just two months later, the mood flipped. The first bandwagon "lobster keepers" were already paying people to uninstall it; MIIT issued a security warning; and tech media turned on it, calling it underpowered and too expensive.

To many industry veterans, this fast-in, fast-out tech frenzy was entirely expected. To put it bluntly: OpenClaw is essentially a toy-grade AI concept machine, worlds away from a real productivity tool.

Why? Today we won't talk about obscure code—just business and common sense.

OpenClaw's viral moment
en.reason: OpenClaw hit 270,000 GitHub stars in two months before collapsing under messy installation, runaway token costs of up to 10,000 yuan a month and a security slip that let it delete Meta's security director's emails.

Within two months it pulled in 270,000 GitHub stars, trampling Linux's all-time record; big tech scrambled for it, it flooded WeChat Moments, and it felt as if you couldn't greet a peer without "raising a lobster."

But the internet's memory is a strange thing.

Just two months later, the mood flipped. The first bandwagon "lobster keepers" were already paying people to uninstall it; MIIT issued a security warning; and tech media turned on it, calling it underpowered and too expensive.

To many industry veterans, this fast-in, fast-out tech frenzy was entirely expected. To put it bluntly: OpenClaw is essentially a toy-grade AI concept machine, worlds away from a real productivity tool.

Why? Today we won't talk about obscure code—just business and common sense.

OpenClaw's viral moment
en.reason: OpenClaw hit 270,000 GitHub stars in two months before collapsing under messy installation, runaway token costs of up to 10,000 yuan a month and a security slip that let it delete Meta's security director's emails.

sources.summary:
AI 生成的前端网页往往充满光斑、渐变与大圆角按钮。本文实测开源设计工具 unslop，通过审计和九轮微调，7 分钟内完成去塑料感重构。
让 AI 做个网页，十个有九个长一个样：蓝色大按钮、带 ✨ 的小标签、背景飘着几团光斑、按钮下面一排绿对勾，一眼就能看出浓浓的模板塑料味。
推倒重来太费劲，自己一处处抠 CSS 又不知道从哪下手。这次我实测了一个专门解决这一问题的开源设计技能：unslop。
先看改动前后的效果对比。上面是豆包一句话生成的「随记」官网，下面是 unslop 在 WorkBuddy 里微调了 7 分钟后的实际呈现：
同一个产品、同一段文案底子，调整后的视觉质感完全脱离了原先的 AI 样板味。
unslop 是开发者 Damir Sokolovsky（GitHub ID: heydamir）开源的一个设计技能包，专治「一看就是 AI 生成的界面」。该仓库于 10 月 29 日建立，到 11 月 18 日已收获 18,330 个 star，增长十分迅速。
它的核心逻辑不是直接让大模型全部重写。它会先进行页面审计，把界面上典型的 AI 套路逐条列出；接着结合产品定位确定独立的
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 实测开源工具 unslop 对豆包生成的「随记」官网做后置审计，列出15项AI套路，九轮微调后仅用6分56秒完成去塑料感重构。

en.title: Using unslop to fix the plastic feel of AI-generated web pages: a 7-minute refactor, tested hands-on
en.summary:
AI-generated front-end pages tend to be stuffed with glows, gradients and big rounded buttons. I tested the open-source design tool unslop, which audited the page and made nine rounds of fine-tuning to strip out the plastic look in seven minutes.

Ask AI to build a webpage and nine out of ten come out looking identical: a big blue button, little tags with ✨, a few blobs of light drifting in the background, a row of green checkmarks under the button — the template plastic look is obvious at a glance.

Starting over is too much work, and picking through the CSS yourself leaves you unsure where to begin. So I tested an open-source design skill built specifically for this problem: unslop.

First, the before and after. Above is a "Notes" landing page generated by Doubao in a single prompt; below is how it actually looked after unslop spent seven minutes fine-tuning it in WorkBuddy:

Same product, same underlying copy — but the adjusted version has completely shed the original AI boilerplate feel.

unslop is an open-source design skill package from developer Damir Sokolovsky (GitHub ID: heydamir), aimed squarely at interfaces that "look obviously AI-generated." The repo was created on October 29 and had 18,330 stars by November 18 — very rapid growth.

Its core logic isn't to have the large model rewrite everything outright. It first runs a page audit, listing the typical AI clichés on the interface one by one; then, combined with the product positioning, it establishes an independent
